142: impl<'s, M: Matcher, S: Sink> MultiLine<'s, M, S> {
143:     pub fn new(
144:         searcher: &'s Searcher,
145:         matcher: M,
146:         slice: &'s [u8],
147:         write_to: S,
148:     ) -> MultiLine<'s, M, S> {
149:         debug_assert!(searcher.multi_line_with_matcher(&matcher));
150: 
151:         MultiLine {
152:             config: &searcher.config,
153:             core: Core::new(searcher, matcher, write_to, true),
154:             slice: slice,
155:             last_match: None,
156:         }
157:     }
158: 
159:     pub fn run(mut self) -> Result<(), S::Error> {
160:         if self.core.begin()? {
161:             let binary_upto =
162:                 cmp::min(self.slice.len(), DEFAULT_BUFFER_CAPACITY);
163:             let binary_range = Range::new(0, binary_upto);
164:             if !self.core.detect_binary(self.slice, &binary_range)? {
165:                 let mut keepgoing = true;
166:                 while !self.slice[self.core.pos()..].is_empty() && keepgoing {
167:                     keepgoing = self.sink()?;
168:                 }
169:                 if keepgoing {
170:                     keepgoing = match self.last_match.take() {
171:                         None => true,
172:                         Some(last_match) => {
173:                             if self.sink_context(&last_match)? {
174:                                 self.sink_matched(&last_match)?;
175:                             }
176:                             true
177:                         }
178:                     };
179:                 }
180:                 // Take care of any remaining context after the last match.
181:                 if keepgoing {
182:                     if self.config.passthru {
183:                         self.core.other_context_by_line(
184:                             self.slice,
185:                             self.slice.len(),
186:                         )?;
187:                     } else {
188:                         self.core.after_context_by_line(
189:                             self.slice,
190:                             self.slice.len(),
191:                         )?;
192:                     }
193:                 }
194:             }
195:         }
196:         let byte_count = self.byte_count();
197:         let binary_byte_offset = self.core.binary_byte_offset();
198:         self.core.finish(byte_count, binary_byte_offset)
199:     }

201:     fn sink(&mut self) -> Result<bool, S::Error> {
202:         if self.config.invert_match {
203:             return self.sink_matched_inverted();
204:         }
205:         let mat = match self.find()? {
206:             Some(range) => range,
207:             None => {
208:                 self.core.set_pos(self.slice.len());
209:                 return Ok(true);
210:             }
211:         };
212:         self.advance(&mat);
213: 
214:         let line =
215:             lines::locate(self.slice, self.config.line_term.as_byte(), mat);
216:         // We delay sinking the match to make sure we group adjacent matches
217:         // together in a single sink. Adjacent matches are distinct matches
218:         // that start and end on the same line, respectively. This guarantees
219:         // that a single line is never sinked more than once.
220:         match self.last_match.take() {
221:             None => {
222:                 self.last_match = Some(line);
223:                 Ok(true)
224:             }
225:             Some(last_match) => {
226:                 // If the lines in the previous match overlap with the lines
227:                 // in this match, then simply grow the match and move on. This
228:                 // happens when the next match begins on the same line that the
229:                 // last match ends on.
230:                 //
231:                 // Note that we do not technically require strict overlap here.
232:                 // Instead, we only require that the lines are adjacent. This
233:                 // provides larger blocks of lines to the printer, and results
234:                 // in overall better behavior with respect to how replacements
235:                 // are handled.
236:                 //
237:                 // See: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1311
238:                 // And also the associated commit fixing #1311.
239:                 if last_match.end() >= line.start() {
240:                     self.last_match = Some(last_match.with_end(line.end()));
241:                     Ok(true)
242:                 } else {
243:                     self.last_match = Some(line);
244:                     if !self.sink_context(&last_match)? {
245:                         return Ok(false);
246:                     }
247:                     self.sink_matched(&last_match)
248:                 }
249:             }
250:         }
251:     }

253:     fn sink_matched_inverted(&mut self) -> Result<bool, S::Error> {
254:         assert!(self.config.invert_match);
255: 
256:         let invert_match = match self.find()? {
257:             None => {
258:                 let range = Range::new(self.core.pos(), self.slice.len());
259:                 self.core.set_pos(range.end());
260:                 range
261:             }
262:             Some(mat) => {
263:                 let line = lines::locate(
264:                     self.slice,
265:                     self.config.line_term.as_byte(),
266:                     mat,
267:                 );
268:                 let range = Range::new(self.core.pos(), line.start());
269:                 self.advance(&line);
270:                 range
271:             }
272:         };
273:         if invert_match.is_empty() {
274:             return Ok(true);
275:         }
276:         if !self.sink_context(&invert_match)? {
277:             return Ok(false);
278:         }
279:         let mut stepper = LineStep::new(
280:             self.config.line_term.as_byte(),
281:             invert_match.start(),
282:             invert_match.end(),
283:         );
284:         while let Some(line) = stepper.next_match(self.slice) {
285:             if !self.sink_matched(&line)? {
286:                 return Ok(false);
287:             }
288:         }
289:         Ok(true)
290:     }

292:     fn sink_matched(&mut self, range: &Range) -> Result<bool, S::Error> {
293:         if range.is_empty() {
294:             // The only way we can produce an empty line for a match is if we
295:             // match the position immediately following the last byte that we
296:             // search, and where that last byte is also the line terminator. We
297:             // never want to report that match, and we know we're done at that
298:             // point anyway, so stop the search.
299:             return Ok(false);
300:         }
301:         self.core.matched(self.slice, range)
302:     }

304:     fn sink_context(&mut self, range: &Range) -> Result<bool, S::Error> {
305:         if self.config.passthru {
306:             if !self.core.other_context_by_line(self.slice, range.start())? {
307:                 return Ok(false);
308:             }
309:         } else {
310:             if !self.core.after_context_by_line(self.slice, range.start())? {
311:                 return Ok(false);
312:             }
313:             if !self.core.before_context_by_line(self.slice, range.start())? {
314:                 return Ok(false);
315:             }
316:         }
317:         Ok(true)
318:     }
319: 
320:     fn find(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Range>, S::Error> {
321:         match self.core.matcher().find(&self.slice[self.core.pos()..]) {
322:             Err(err) => Err(S::Error::error_message(err)),
323:             Ok(None) => Ok(None),
324:             Ok(Some(m)) => Ok(Some(m.offset(self.core.pos()))),
325:         }
326:     }

328:     /// Advance the search position based on the previous match.
329:     ///
330:     /// If the previous match is zero width, then this advances the search
331:     /// position one byte past the end of the match.
332:     fn advance(&mut self, range: &Range) {
333:         self.core.set_pos(range.end());
334:         if range.is_empty() && self.core.pos() < self.slice.len() {
335:             let newpos = self.core.pos() + 1;
336:             self.core.set_pos(newpos);
337:         }
338:     }

341:         match self.core.binary_byte_offset() {
342:             Some(offset) if offset < self.core.pos() as u64 => offset,
343:             _ => self.core.pos() as u64,
344:         }
345:     }
346: }

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `Replacer::replace_all` (crates/printer/src/util.rs:89): in `--multiline` mode, the printer performs replacements by re-running the matcher over the buffer, which extends up to `MAX_LOOK_AHEAD` bytes past the reported match range to accommodate look-around. Since `replace_with_captures_at` had no end bound, the find-iterator would discover *additional* matches beyond the reported match, and all the in-between buffer text was copied into the replacement output — expanding what got printed.

The fix adds a bounded `replace_with_captures_in_context` helper that only replaces matches starting before `range.end` and copies trailing bytes only up to `range.end`, mirroring how `find_iter_at_in_context` already bounds match discovery.

Validation:
- `cargo test --workspace`: all tests pass (including all printer/searcher suites)
- Reproduced the issue's exact command against a rebuilt `rg`: `-r '$usage'` now outputs only ` [-h] [-U|-u <pkgspec>,...] [...] [-- <pip-compile-arg>...]`, matching the non-`-r` match content.
